summary: RestService.getResourceBySupportedClass() ignores order when resources with different names share a supportedClass
description:
RestServiceImpl.initializeResources() builds two lookup maps while scanning @Resource-annotated classes:
resourceDefinitionsByNames (keyed by resource name) — correctly arbitrates between colliding definitions using order via isResourceToBeAdded().

resourcesBySupportedClasses (keyed by supported class) — has no such arbitration. When two resources with different names declare the same supportedClass, whichever is scanned last simply overwrites the map entry, regardless of order.

Because ConversionUtil.getConverter(Class) and RestService.getResourceBySupportedClass(Class) both read from resourcesBySupportedClasses, a resource from one module can be silently and non-deterministically replaced by an unrelated, differently-named resource from another module that happens to support the same domain class — even when the replaced resource has a lower (better) order and would win a same-name comparison.
Core's own MainResourceController.retrieve() resolves resources by name (resourceDefinitionsByNames), so it's unaffected. Any custom code that resolves by class instead  — directly via getResourceBySupportedClass(), or indirectly via ConversionUtil.getConverter() — is exposed to this bug, and which resource "wins" depends on module load/scan order, making it hard to reproduce and easy to break silently when a new module is added.
We noticed this when writing an ExtendedObsResource (name=v1/obs, order=0) in one of our modules, which was being silently clobbered in resourcesBySupportedClasses by an unrelated coreapps resource (LatestObsResource, different name, same supportedClass=Obs.class, worse order), breaking custom Obs conversion logic in a REST controller that resolved its converter by class — with no error, just wrong output.  Adding to this problematic behavior is that it seemed to be environmental - i.e. in my local SDK the correct resource was retrieved, but when deployed to a test server, a different resource was returned.
Fix: apply the same order-based arbitration already used for resourceDefinitionsByNames to resourcesBySupportedClasses, so a resource can't be clobbered by a worse-ordered, differently-named resource for the same class.
